newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Statement on China troop entry into Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Statement on China troop entry into Hong Kong.

text.p: Beijing will send 4,000 troops with helicopters and armoured cars into Hong Kong on July 1, just hours after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule.
The following is the full text of a statement on the troop movements issued on Friday by the office of Hong Kong's chief executive designate, Tung Chee-hwa:
The HKSAR (Hong Kong Special Administrative Region) Chief Executive's Office was informed today about the arrangements for the entry into Hong Kong of the People's Liberation Army (PLA) Garrison.

A spokesman for the CE's Office welcomed the news and said the first group of 509 military personnel being the advance elements would arrive in Hong Kong from Shenzhen via Huanggang Port in 39 vehicles at 9 p.m. (2100 local/1300 GMT) on June 30.
They would be stationed at the Prince of Wales Barracks, Stanley Fort, Stonecutters Island and Shek Kong Camp, and would take up their duties at midnight, he said.

The second group of about 4,000 personnel, who form the main contingent of the PLA Garrison in Hong Kong, will arrive at 6 a.m. on July 1 by land, sea and air routes in 10 ships, six helicopters, 21 armoured cars and 400 other vehicles.
The land forces will use three routes: 28 vehicles will enter through Sha Tau Kok; 174 vehicles at Man Kam To; and 215 vehicles at Huanggang.
The 10 naval vessels will enter from the west in two formations and sail to Stonecutters Island.
The helicopters will fly over Man Kam To control point to Shek Kong air base.
The HKSAR Government will make suitable arrangements to facilitate the arrival of the PLA Garrison to carry out its duties in Hong Kong.
